<reason>A won by making the debate easier to decide: the motion’s net-loss claim needs a reason this wave breaks the historical elasticity pattern, and B’s cost-cutting adoption story was the same mechanism that previously expanded employment. B had a coherent “copyable cognition fills extra demand” theory and a real lag argument, but conceded no market yet shows net white-collar decline and slipped toward a weaker “halfway fail” policy bar. A answered the non-liability occupations with demand expansion plus monitoring triggers, so worry never became a forecast.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A’s reply that firms always adopt automation to cut headcount (tractors, looms, spreadsheets) yet jobs still grew, so that mechanism cannot by itself prove elasticity has run out.</best_rebuttal>
